s1.syndrome_frame: Acute heart failure with signs of volume overload and possible restrictive cardiomyopathy
salient_findings: New-onset heart failure symptoms 2 weeks after COVID-19 vaccination booster
Signs of volume overload with lower-extremity edema and jugular venous distention
Elevated N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide and abnormal echocardiogram findings
key_facts: 59-year-old man with history of hypertension and medication-induced diabetes
New-onset heart failure symptoms began 2 weeks after COVID-19 vaccination booster
Clinical examination revealed signs of volume overload
Lower-extremity edema present
Jugular venous distention present
Blood urea nitrogen: 46 mg/dL
Creatinine: 1.79 mg/dL
Uric acid: 14.1 mg/dL
N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide: 206 ng/dL
Echocardiogram showed left ventricular ejection fraction: 64%
Right ventricular dysfunction present
Increased inferior vena cava size: 28 mm with reduced inspiratory collapse
Mild tricuspid regurgitation present
Cardiac MRI showed thickened pericardium greater than 40 mm
Evidence of ventricular interdependence and septal bounce on cardiac MRI

shortlist.label: Constrictive pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Thickened pericardium and signs of volume overload

shortlist.label: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical examination and echocardiogram findings consistent with restrictive physiology

shortlist.label: COVID-19 vaccine-associated myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: New-onset heart failure symptoms began 2 weeks after COVID-19 vaccination booster

shortlist.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Right ventricular dysfunction and possible restrictive cardiomyopathy

shortlist.label: Primary cardiac amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Echocardiogram and cardiac MRI findings suggestive of infiltrative cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging studies, including the thickened pericardium greater than 40 mm on cardiac MRI and evidence of ventricular interdependence and septal bounce, are consistent with constrictive pericarditis. The clinical examination revealing signs of volume overload, such as lower-extremity edema and jugular venous distention, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Restrictive cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: While restrictive cardiomyopathy can present with similar symptoms, the imaging studies specifically showing a thickened pericardium point more towards constrictive pericarditis.

rejected.label: COVID-19 vaccine-associated myocarditis
rejected.why: Myocarditis would typically present with a reduced left ventricular ejection fraction, which is not the case here (64%).

rejected.label: Cardiac sarcoidosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided in the case that would suggest cardiac sarcoidosis, such as granulomas on biopsy or specific findings on imaging.

rejected.label: Primary cardiac amyloidosis
rejected.why: The case does not provide evidence of amyloid deposits or other specific findings that would be characteristic of primary cardiac amyloidosis.
